title: Instruction books and moving from C melody to alto
summary: Mikell's basic training used a Vereecken book, and Willie the Lion told him to switch to alto.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Now what form did his instruction take; that is, what was it that he had you doing?

Oh, he had me ... the usual basic training, you know, to learn an instrument, he gets you a book. The book that I used at that time was the Ben Verekin book which is still a very good book today, and I think to get a 1917 copyright on it, I think, the last time I looked at it.

Can you remember any other instructional books? There's another famous one that's been republished and re-edited from time to time by a man named Paul Deville, which has come under various covers, which is a gigantic, ...
No, I'm not familiar with that at all.
maybe the late 19th century, but it's been re-edited, but you do mention the Ben [Verekin] book.
But this would have been basically more just about the -- I mean just the basic approach to the saxophone. Would this be the Alto Saxophone or still the C Melody?
This was ... by this time, I had probably gone to the C Melo -- I mean to the Alto.

Now let me see ... because, I started out with the C Melody and then I went to the Alto later, after I worked some time with Willie 'The Lion' Smith and the trio, and Willie told me if I expected to play with bands, I'd have to get an Alto, because there was no music being written for the C Melody; you know, orchestral parts. And he was quite right. At that time. If you played with the saxophone section, you had to play Alto or Tenor.
Was the C Melody of any particular value to a beginner in any way; I mean, the fact that it's in C -- is that important in itself?
Well, I didn't think of it as being important at the time, other than it was the instrument that
Trumbauer Frankie Tromburg played, and it was the instrument that was on sale at this pawn shop where they, you know, where they would trade me for the trumpet that I couldn't play over the weekend.
